newsitem.title: GERMANY: Salomon Bros rates VW top Euro auto pick.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Bros rates VW top Euro auto pick.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG was rated top European auto stock for 1997 by Salomon Brothers in a report on the global auto industry, the U.S. investment bank said on Friday.

"We rated Volkswagen as best pick for 1997 and we have it on a buy," Salomon Bros' London-based European auto analyst John Lawson told Reuters, citing currency benefits as one of the reasons for his bullish outlook on the stock.
Lawson said that his colleagues in the U.S. and Asia had rated General Motors and Honda in their respective markets as best picks for 1997.
Salomon Bros rates VW top pick of Euro auto =2
Shares in Volkswagen ended bourse trade in Frankfurt up 3.50 marks, or 0.45 percent, at 769.50 marks, while the overall market ended 1.16 percent lower at 2,998.24 points.
Earlier in the day, dealers said that the Salomon report brought VW buy orders in its wake.
VW's competitors did not fare so well. BMW AG ended bourse down 37 marks at 1,038 marks, while Daimler-Benz AG ended down 1.95 marks at 114.10 marks.
